# Photography & film guide

<!-- Generated by scripts/media-guide.mjs from content/media.ts. Edit the manifest, then run `npm run media:guide`. -->

This is the brief for the professional photography and film that a finished site is built on. Every frame on the template has a slot; each slot below says what to shoot, where it appears, the shape and size it must be delivered at, who is on camera, and how much it matters.

The demonstration edition fills these slots with imagery created from Eric Jokl's likeness so a client can see the finished standard. **A client's own site is built with real professional photography shot to this guide.**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Slots** | 42 (41 photographs, 1 film) |
| **Essential** | 10: the site should not launch without these |
| **Important** | 15: shoot on the main day |
| **Completes the set** | 17: a second half-day, or replace over time |
| **Chef on camera** | 16 frames need the chef or the chef's hands; group them into one session |

To see every slot in place on the live site, open any page with `?notes=1` (or press **N**, or use *Production notes* in the footer). Each frame then shows the file it expects and whether it has been delivered.

---

## 1. The standard

The reference is the photography of Aman, Nobu Hospitality and Casa Cipriani: editorial, quiet, expensive. It should read as a film still from a beautiful evening, never as a menu photograph or an event recap.

| | Do | Never |
|---|---|---|
| **Light** | One warm practical source as the key (candle, pendant, fire, window at blue hour). Deep falloff into shadow. Shoot at the edges of the day. | Flash, on-camera light, flat overhead light, mixed colour temperatures. |
| **Lens & depth** | Prime lenses (35mm, 50mm, 85mm) wide open, f/1.4–f/2.8. One sharp subject, everything else soft. | Wide-angle distortion, everything in focus, phone portrait mode. |
| **Colour** | Espresso, walnut, ivory linen, aged brass, deep oxblood. Warm but true skin and food. One consistent grade across the series. | Teal-and-orange presets, heavy HDR, oversaturated food, cool fluorescent casts. |
| **Food** | At table height, on ivory china, dark stone, linen or walnut. Real steam, real sauce, a fork or glass for scale. | Overhead flat-lays, piled garnish, glossy styling sprays, plastic props. |
| **People** | The chef, the chef's hands, and guests only as backs, hands, shoulders and blur. | Identifiable guests, posed group shots, stock smiles, staff looking into the lens unless briefed. |
| **Places** | Rooms that feel lived in and private. | House numbers, boat names, tail numbers, logos, recognisable landmarks, anything that identifies a client's home. |

## 2. Delivery

**Photographs**
- Shoot RAW. Deliver a graded, retouched master per slot plus the RAW selects.
- Web master: JPEG at quality 90 (or lossless WebP/AVIF), **sRGB**, long edge 3000px or larger, at the exact ratio listed for the slot. The site generates every smaller size itself.
- File name is the slot id: `public/media/<slot>.jpg`. Nothing else is needed; the next build places it.
- Retouching: clean distractions, keep texture. No skin smoothing, no reshaping food, no added steam.
- Strip location metadata before delivery.

**Films**
- Capture in 4K at 24 or 25 fps on a locked-off tripod or a very slow, motivated move. No handheld shake, no speed ramps.
- Deliver 1920×1080: `<slot>.mp4` (H.264, high profile) and `<slot>.webm` (VP9), **no audio track**, 10–15 seconds, seamless loop (the last frame must cut invisibly to the first). Target under 2 MB each.
- Deliver the first frame as `<slot>-poster.jpg` (the `hero-film-poster` slot for the hero). Visitors on slow connections or with reduced motion only ever see this still.

**Rights**
- Signed model release for the chef and anyone whose hands or back appear.
- Signed property release for every home, yacht, hangar or venue, including permission for web and social use.
- Perpetual, worldwide web and social licence for the client, with credit to the photographer on the privacy page if requested.

## 3. Shot list

### Home · the hero

The first screen. It decides whether a visitor keeps reading.

| File | Where it appears | Shape and size | On camera | Priority | What to capture |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hero-figure.jpg` | Home hero — Eric standing right of the name (on phones, above it) | 2:3 transparent cutout, 1024×1536+ | Chef on camera | Essential | Supplied by Eric and live. Three-quarter length, hands in pockets, looking into camera, transparent background. |
| `hero-film.mp4` + `.webm` | Home hero, behind the figure (optional) | 16:9, 1920×1080, 10–15s silent loop, under 2 MB WebM + MP4 | No people | Completes the set | Pure atmosphere behind the figure: candle flames and steam in a dark kitchen, out of focus. No people. |
| `hero-film-poster.jpg` | Home hero — the first frame of hero-film, shown until the film plays and on slow connections | 16:9, 1920×1080 (the film's opening frame) | No people | Completes the set | Export the first frame of the hero film as a still, so the hand-off from photograph to film is invisible. |
| `hero-still.jpg` | Home hero — full-bleed room behind the name and the figure (when there is no film) | 16:9 landscape, 2400×1350+ (the name sits on the left third — keep it dark) | No people | Important | A dark, candlelit dining room set for dinner, no people, the left third deep in shadow so the name reads over it. |

## 4. Planning the shoot

Group the list by light, not by page. A typical schedule for one location with the chef present:

| When | Setup | Slots |
|---|---|---|
| Morning, window light | Kitchen counter: hands, pasta, classes, the market | `exp-kitchen-lessons`, `gallery-04`, `gallery-06`, `gallery-11`, `food-market`, `chapter-hands` |
| Late afternoon | Food at the table: every dish, styled and shot in sequence | `menu-after-midnight`, `menu-late-summer-outdoors`, `menu-at-anchor`, `menu-by-the-fire`, `gallery-01`, `gallery-05`, `gallery-07`, `gallery-09`, `gallery-12`, `food-table` |
| Golden hour | Outdoors: lawn, terrace, the water | `exp-island-water`, `room-estate`, `room-waterfront`, `room-yacht`, `room-island`, `room-abroad`, `chapter-distance` |
| Blue hour into night | Dining room and kitchen by candle and pendant: portraits, the pass, the room, the hero | `hero-figure`, `hero-film`, `hero-film-poster`, `hero-still`, `portrait`, `exp-private-table`, `exp-occasion`, `gallery-02`, `gallery-03`, `gallery-08`, `gallery-10`, `food-pass`, `room-residence`, `room-penthouse`, `room-hangar`, `chapter-patience`, `chapter-fire`, `chapter-room`, `chapter-tonight` |

Shoot the **Essential** slots first in every setup. If the day runs short, everything marked *Completes the set* can follow later without the site ever looking unfinished: an empty slot shows a lit, grained study in the same mood, never a grey box.

## 5. Acceptance checklist

Before a frame goes live, it should pass every line:

- [ ] Exactly the ratio listed for its slot, 3000px or more on the long edge, sRGB.
- [ ] One warm key light, deep shadow, no flash, no overhead flat-lay.
- [ ] One sharp subject; the rest falls away.
- [ ] No identifiable guest, no logo, no house number, boat name or tail number.
- [ ] Grade matches the rest of the series side by side.
- [ ] Seen in place with `?notes=1` on desktop **and** a phone; nothing important is cropped by the frame or covered by type.
- [ ] Releases on file.
